title: ProductionRunManifest
description: The AUDIT RECORD of ONE serial production run (roadmap Phase 5.5). run_serial (runtime/serialize/) drives the production chain over a planned chapter sequence — build → execute(Brain) → project state — and returns a rich in-memory result (per-chapter outcome, draft/state hashes, verdicts, skips, pacing) that, before this manifest, was printed and discarded. This artifact persists that result as a governable record: what a run produced (artifacts + output paths + draft hashes), what it skipped and why (failures), what it cost (model-calls + token usage + money, folded from each produced chapter's persisted produced_by.llm block), what it staged for human approval (publish_readiness), and enough pins (draft_hash + state_hash + prompt_version + model params + replay_ref) to REPRODUCE the run. REPRODUCIBILITY STANCE, mirroring the build manifest (manifest.py): the DRAFTS a run produces are byte-reproducible (each carries a content_hash pinned to its package + source versions), but THIS manifest is a time-stamped audit record — it embeds started_at/finished_at and live cost/latency, so it is deliberately NOT byte-reproducible and must never be hashed as if it were. Two disciplines hold: `gating` const false — a run manifest is an audit record, it never gates a build (ADR-003); and it is written to registry/derived/run-manifests/, NEVER to registry/facts/ (a production record is not a story fact, and runtime/serialize/ is not a fact-writer — only runtime/mint/ is, ADR-006, fitness guard #10). HONEST SCOPE: cost/token data exists only for chapters produced by a LIVE model; a deterministic-stub run records cost null and live_calls 0 (the stub sets no token/cost metadata), so the manifest never fabricates costs it did not incur.

id.description: Manifest-local audit id (like MINT-/FCP-/RCP-). NOT an entity id — it names a production event, not a story fact, so it is not allocated through the ID Mint Ledger.

gating.description: Structural invariant (ADR-003): a run manifest is an audit record, not a build gate. The serial it records never gates either — a chapter that fails its own deterministic gate is skipped, the run goes on.

run.description: The run's parameters + wall-clock bounds. started_at/finished_at are timestamps (why this manifest is not byte-reproducible).

started_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC time the run began.

finished_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC time the run finished.

prompt_version.description: The chapter-draft prompt template MAJOR version used (1.0.0 plain, 2.0.0 story-so-far, 3/4/5 scene/IR/character).

commercial.description: Whether the per-chapter Commercial Optimization Loop (P16) ran.

panel.description: The reader panel for --commercial (appetite/commercial/both), when commercial ran.

model_provider.description: The generation model provider (deterministic when the stub produced the drafts).

model_id.description: The generation model id, when a live provider was used.

max_chapters.description: The cap on chapters produced this run, if any.

totals.description: Run-level roll-ups folded from the chapters.

planned.description: Chapters in the plan this run attempted.

produced.description: Chapters that completed (a draft was written).

skipped.description: Chapters skipped (build or per-chapter gate failed) — the run's failures.

final_state_hash.description: The StoryState fold hash after the last produced chapter (ADR-008).

live_calls.description: Chapters whose draft was produced by a LIVE model (carried a produced_by.llm block). 0 for a deterministic-stub run.

token_usage.description: Summed token usage across live-model chapters. All zero when no live model ran.

cost.description: Summed money cost across live-model chapters, or null when no live model ran (the deterministic stub incurs no cost — never fabricated).

chapters.description: One entry per attempted chapter, produced or skipped, in run order.

event.description: The event id this chapter dramatizes.

ok.description: Whether the chapter was produced (false = skipped).

stage.description: The stage reached (done, or build:*/execute:* for a skip).

message.description: Detail — populated for skips (the failure reason).

draft_hash.description: The produced draft's content_hash (byte-reproducible; a reproduction pin).

state_hash.description: The StoryState fold hash as of this chapter (ADR-008).

verdict.description: The chapter's evaluative QA verdict (advisory, never gated).

commercial_verdict.description: The Commercial Optimization Loop verdict (comparison-only), when commercial ran.

output_path.description: The persisted draft envelope's path under registry/derived/ (the output artifact).

llm.description: The model-call record folded from the produced draft's produced_by.llm. Null for a skipped chapter or a deterministic-stub draft.

replay_ref.description: The replay cache ref — a reproduction pin for this call.

publish_readiness.description: The 'Build Gate ≠ Publish Readiness' verdict folded from the chapter's envelope (Phase 4.1) — the run's staged approvals. Never gates the build; a human-authority decision (ADR-009). Null when not assessed.

chapter_final.description: The chapter-final derived artifact folded from registry/derived/chapter-final/ for this chapter, when present.

serial_pacing.description: The cross-chapter climax-rhythm check over the run's produced chapters (advisory, never gates). Null when fewer than two enriched chapters existed.

rationale.description: Human-readable summary (n produced, m skipped, cost).
